# User Reports — Periodic RA Spikes Near 110–160 s

**Dimension:** first-hand reports of periodic RA spikes on the EQ6-R / EQ6-R Pro and close
relatives, what was tried, and what (if anything) fixed them. Sources:
[citations.md](../citations.md). All are Tier 4 (forum / mailing list) unless noted.

## Closest matches to a 134–138 s, ~7" spike

1. **Case A — the only resolved match on a Sky-Watcher EQ6-family mount.** Dan Watt's EQ6
   "started a fun new RA spike every 133 seconds" about a year after he "replaced the
   bearings with better ones from deepspaceproducts" [15]. Every belt, pulley, motor and
   adjustment change failed. Final post: "It was the "upgraded" ceramic worm gear bearings.
   While I couldn't feel or hear any difference, when I popped the original 608 bearings
   back in all of my weird spikes disappeared and I'm back to guiding at .4 RMS." [15]
   - Caveats: legacy EQ6 (47:12 motor stage), not EQ6-R; same 180:1 worm and 478.7 s worm
     period [15]. Ceramic bearing brand/geometry never stated. Period measured while guiding;
     OzAndrewJ cautioned "the 133 seconds may be affected by the act of guiding" [15].
2. **Case B — same period and shape, different brand.** "Every ~134s the error goes from
   within ~1.5 arc-sec to over 5 (and sometimes as high as 9) arc-sec. It recovers very
   quickly, usually within a second or two." [16] Fixed after belt re-centring/tensioning,
   worm-gear tightening, re-plugging the RA serial cable and redoing polar alignment; which
   change mattered is unknown. Hoskin's attribution to "the
   small pulley of the belt drive" [16] was asserted, not derived.
3. **Case C — EQ6-R Pro at 133 s, unresolved.** Brian Valente (PHD2 team) identified
   "large harmonic periodic error at 133 seconds and 67 seconds" and pointed to "spur gears,
   belt, etc." [18]. A new RA motor did not help [18]. Bearings were not tested.
4. **Case D — EQ6R Pro, fast ~6" spike.** Andy Galasso (PHD2 Log Viewer author): "a rapid
   spike of about 6" that occurs about every 120s … cannot be guided out" [17]. John Sim read
   the same log as a 109.2 s fundamental from its harmonic series [17]. Period disagreement
   between two analysts of one log is itself evidence of FFT-reading uncertainty.

## Patterns across cases

- **Motor-pulley faults sit at ~120 s on the EQ6-R** (cases D, E, F; [20][21][22][26]). The
  user's 134–138 s is outside that.
- **Replacing the RA motor did not fix a 133 s spike** (C) [18]; neither did motor/pulley
  swaps in A [15].
- **Bearing involvement is raised in four independent threads**: confirmed in A [15],
  suspected for the 160 s line in E [20], and suggested as worm-bearing brinelling in G [26], and suspected for an AZ-EQ6 ±20" worm-period pulse, where a pulley touching the casting was also offered as a cause [23].
- **Resolutions that worked were mechanical and specific**: worm-bearing replacement (A),
  belt/worm slop (B), worm mesh backed off (J). No firmware or software fix is reported (D, C).

## Gaps and limitations

- Cases A and B are not EQ6-R Pro mounts. No fetched source documents a resolved 130–140 s
  spike on an EQ6-R Pro.
- Spike amplitudes in A, C, E, F, G are only in images that were not captured.
- Two requested threads were not supplied: Cloudy Nights 711487 and 972954. AstroBin 85441
  page 3 (a T. Spofford 240 s pulley case, per page index) was not read.
- Search coverage: every query ran on a single web engine (Yahoo); see
